title: Ideological Origins of World War II
text:
# Ideological Origins of World War II

Oxford University Press eBooks. Published: 2023-05-22. Book chapter. 0 citations.

## Abstract

Abstract The chapter explores the role played by the most influential revolutionary movements of the past century, Communism and Fascism, alongside Japanese ultra-nationalism in fueling the tumult of the interwar period that led to World War II. It highlights the conflict among colonialisms, as Britain and France tried to keep the world unchanged under the pressure from post-1933 Germany, Mussolini’s dreams of Mediterranean empire, and Japan’s anti-Western push for imperial and racial hegemony across East Asia. The analysis explains the historical, divine mission intrinsic to images of the upcoming war among revisionist powers—Germany, Italy, Japan, and the Soviet Union. These challengers of the status-quo mobilized contestation throughout the world that subverted domestic orders and international hierarchies. The war brought unprecedented radicalization—achieving the right form of modernity became a matter of life or death. Such realignment of the globe was, until 1989–1991, the legacy of World War II and of its ideological origins.
